findings.issue: The fix for the unknown owner sends sellerId null on the StockLine, which is correct. It also stores null on the order item. Inventory's controller then resolves the real owner S through SellerDirectory and reserves S's offer-tagged rows. The returned Allocation carries sellerId S, but Order.attach (Order.java:776, 799-800) ignores al.sellerId(), defaults the item to PLATFORM_SELLER, and tags it that way. Result: seller S's stock is consumed while the shipment, seller visibility and the seller-service sale booking go to PLATFORM. In practice this path is unreachable because product.offers.seller_id is NOT NULL (V7), and before this change the same case was booked to PLATFORM anyway (it took platform stock then). Not exploitable, but it is a latent ledger mismatch.
findings.fix: In Order.attach, when item.getSellerId() is null, take the seller from al.sellerId() (fall back to PLATFORM_SELLER only when the allocation has none). Alternatively, reject an offer line with an unknown owner at placement with PRODUCT_UNAVAILABLE.

findings.issue: When a sellerId is supplied, inventory trusts it without checking it against the offer's real owner. A caller holding the internal token that sends sellerId=PLATFORM with a seller's offerId (one with no rows) gets that line served from platform stock. Only order-service calls this endpoint, and it derives sellerId from product-service, so this is defense in depth within the existing /internal/** trust model, not a reachable buyer path.
findings.fix: Optional hardening for the backlog: when sellerId==PLATFORM and the offerId lookup finds no offer-tagged rows, confirm ownership through SellerDirectory.offer before the transaction, or have inventory record offer ownership on the stock write.

summary: No blocker or major issues. Fail-closed reservation: ReservationService falls back to platform rows, and to UNLIMITED, only when the line's owner is exactly Platform.SELLER_ID. A seller offer, an unknown owner (null, or a 404 from SellerDirectory) and a stale or orphan offerId all end in OutOfStockException. Seller rows that fall short are never topped up from platform stock. A buyer cannot pick another seller's stock beyond buying that seller's offer: chooseOffer limits offerIds to those on the product, rows are found by offer_id, and a mismatched productId/offerId pair finds no rows. The owner lookup runs before @Transactional reserve, so no HTTP call holds row locks, and an outage raises UpstreamUnavailableException (503, which names only the upstream) before any stock changes. Ownership cannot change, so there is no TOCTOU window. Row locks plus the new 20-thread integration test cover reserve concurrency. Forged inventory events: product-service still drops every QUANTITY_CHANGED that carries an offerId. Prices sync after commit by pulling from product-service, not from the event payload. A forged seller-scoped event can only trigger a cart back-in-stock alert, which is the existing Kafka trust model. The new event fields are UUIDs and a quantity, with no PII; the log line carries productId and offerId only. offerTotal uses bound parameters, so there is no injection. Slice-1 minors: #1 is resolved (a ValidationException, including a mapped inventory 400/403, no longer triggers zeroStock, and createOffer validates quantity>=0 before offerService.create). #2 is resolved for reservation (sellerId is null for an unknown owner), with the order-item booking follow-up in finding 1. #3 and #4 remain filed as B-6 and B-7. No dependency additions and no secrets.
